steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Grouped data organises values into class intervals. When class intervals have different widths, we need special techniques to represent them fairly.

steps.title: Higher Tier Only
steps.body: Histograms with unequal class intervals and cumulative frequency graphs are Higher tier topics. You must understand frequency density.

steps.title: When class widths are equal
steps.body: The height of each bar represents the frequency directly. Bars touch each other (no gaps).

steps.title: Key Formula
steps.body: Frequency Density = Frequency ÷ Class Width The area of each bar represents the frequency, not the height!

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: A histogram bar has width 25 and frequency density 3.2. Find the frequency. | Calculate the frequency density for a class with width 15 and frequency 45. | A cumulative frequency graph has total 200. What cumulative frequency gives the median?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Histograms have NO gaps between bars (continuous data) For unequal class intervals, always calculate frequency density Area of bar = frequency (not height!) Cumulative frequency graphs start at (0, 0) or the lowest boundary Use the graph to find median, quartiles, and percentiles Read scales carefully - cumulative frequency graphs have different scales
